method: Hand-authored. Each rule was written by reading the OpenStax section title against the AAMC topic list for the candidate content category (both are in outline.json). Rules are matched most-specific-first: an exact section number, then the chapter, then nothing. A page that matches no rule is unattributed, and unattributed is a reported outcome rather than a gap to be filled.
why_not_automatic: Keyword scoring over the AAMC topic lists was tried on paper and rejected. It attributes confidently and wrongly: 'Regulation of Body Processes' scores on 'regulation' against 1D's metabolic regulation, and photosynthesis scores on 'electron transport chain' against 1D, which the MCAT does not test. A wrong attribution is worse than none, because it silently poisons both coverage and the category filter retrieval runs.

confidence_levels.high: The section's subject matter appears by name in the AAMC topic list for this category.
confidence_levels.medium: The subject matter is clearly within the category's remit, but is not itemised by AAMC or is only part of what the section covers.
confidence_levels.low: Defensible but contestable. Treat category-filtered retrieval over these as weaker evidence.

known_gaps: Sensory reception (chapter 36) is left unattributed. The Outline puts sensing the environment in PS 6A, outside the demo section, while BB 3A covers nervous system structure. Attributing a biology textbook's sensory chapters to a psychology category was judged unreliable, so nothing is claimed.

Lipid structure (3.3) is left unattributed. AAMC lists 'Lipids (BC, OC): description; structure; steroids' under 3A, alongside the nervous and endocrine systems. That placement is real but reads as an error to any reviewer checking the map, so the section is left unattributed rather than filed somewhere indefensible.

General chemistry (chapters 1-2: atoms, water, carbon) is left unattributed. It belongs to CP 4E, 5A and 5B, and this corpus does not index the Chem/Phys section; attributing a Bio book's chunks to CP categories would make Chem/Phys coverage look supported by a source that was never ingested for it.
Photosynthesis (chapter 8), phylogenetics (20), biological diversity (23-32) and ecology (44-47) are left unattributed because the Outline does not test them.

Genomics and proteomics (17.2, 17.4, 17.5) are left unattributed. 1B lists DNA sequencing and analysis of gene expression, but the sections are mostly about genome projects and bioinformatics, which it does not.

The Outline's 3B lists a skin system and a lymphatic system. Biology 1e covers both only in passing, inside chapters 33 and 42, so retrieval for those topics will be thin. Nothing is misattributed to compensate.
